■ The Visionary Modernist: The Life of Poet Minoru Yoshioka

In the post-war Japanese poetry scene, Minoru Yoshioka is known as a representative poet of modernist poetry, characterized by surrealistic visions. The lines of poetry he spun were filled with dreamlike and phantasmagoric imagery, sometimes described as difficult to understand. Yet, they continue to exude a mysterious charm that leaves a strong impression on the hearts of readers.

In real life, while working as an editor and book designer for a publishing company after the war, Yoshioka continued to write poetry. His avant-garde style attracted the attention of artists in other fields of his time, such as the butoh dancer Tatsumi Hijikata and the playwright Shuji Terayama. Furthermore, younger poets like Kazuko Shiraishi and Gozo Yoshimasu were also greatly influenced by Yo
■ Childhood: A Boy from the Downtown, Awakening to Literature

Minoru Yoshioka was born in 1919 in Honjo, Tokyo (present-day Sumida Ward). It is said that his father worked as a janitor at Meitoku Elementary School and there was not a single book in their home. During the Great Kanto Earthquake, he experienced various hardships, such as contracting pneumonia while evacuated, but as the youngest child, he was very much loved by his parents. Growing up in an en

In his teens, Yoshioka began writing poetry himself. Initially, he boldly tackled traditional fixed-form poetry such as waka and haiku. He was particularly stimulated by the avant-garde haiku of Akio Tomizawa and became strongly attracted to the works of pre-war Japanese modernist poets. Furthermore, he encountered the avant-garde poetry of Katsue Kitazono and Chika Sagawa, and was greatly influen

Eventually, exchanges with literary friends began to emerge. In 1938, after leaving Nanzando, Yoshioka took shelter at the "Yumekashu Shojuku," a private school run by his acquaintance, the writer Huryo Sato, and became a student, honing his poetry and writing. Through such self-study and interaction, the foundation as a poet was cultivated within Minoru Yoshioka.
